prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1119; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling westbound on a multi-lane arterial in Sugar Land, Texas, and was turning left into a commercial lot when the vehicle was struck on the driver side by Driver 2, who was proceeding straight through the intersection. Driver 1 was operating a vehicle in which the Passenger was also seated. Responding officers observed that the vehicle sustained front-end and driver-side damage that appears broadly consistent with the reported impact sequence. Photographs taken at the scene support several of the details provided by both drivers. No independent witnesses were located, and no statements could be obtained from anyone other than the parties involved. Both the officer and the parties at the scene confirmed that the Passenger was inside the vehicle at the time of the collision. Driver 1 reported a wrist injury and was transported for evaluation, though it is not yet clear whether that injury resulted from this crash. Records reviewed at the scene showed no prior damage to the vehicle. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle.
